implementation_notes: Rust has no inherited stateless base to optimize away: a struct with no fields is a zero-sized type, and the Reference guarantees zero-sized types have size 0 and that PhantomData<T> is exactly size_of == 0 with alignment 1, while taking no storage inside enclosing aggregates. Type parameters that exist only for static analysis are carried with PhantomData instead of a real field - it costs nothing and still tells the compiler about ownership, variance, drop check and auto traits - and #[repr(transparent)] keeps a wrapper's ABI identical to its single non-zero field. The classic decision survives only as a choice of carrier: put stateless policy in a generic parameter or a ZST field, never in a field that has real size.
pitfalls: References to ZSTs must still be non-null and aligned, and offsetting a ZST pointer is a no-op, so unsafe code must not treat ZST addresses as identity or allocate for them.
PhantomData is not a neutral placeholder: its type parameter changes variance, drop-check and auto traits (Send/Sync), so PhantomData<T> and PhantomData<*const T> are different decisions.
A zero-sized generic parameter is free in memory but monomorphises code per type, so the cost moves from data to binary size and compile time.
